title: Urology and Continence Supply Program claim denials and appeals by denial code
content:
On the Urology and Continence Supply Program a denial is worked by its denial code, and the code alone decides the route. The Continence Self-Pay Program has no denials or appeals.

## Routes by denial code

| Code | Meaning | Route |
|---|---|---|
| CO-16 | claim lacks information | Unprocessable, never appealed. It is cured only by a corrected claim transmitted no later than the tier's corrected-claim window, in calendar days after the denial's posting date. |
| CO-50 | not medically necessary | Appealable. |
| CO-151 | frequency or quantity not supported | Appealable only when a medical record supporting the quantity, dated on or before the date of service, is on file. |
| CO-197 | authorization absent | Appealable only when an authorization grant valid on the date of service is on file. |
| CO-29 | timely filing expired | Never appealed and never billed to the customer. Larkfield writes it off with a billing-correction adjustment. |
| PR-204 | not covered under the plan | Becomes the customer's responsibility only under the liability notice rule. Otherwise Larkfield absorbs it. |

**CO-197 and CO-151 without the record they need.** Otherwise the denial is not appealed and is handled as a non-covered amount under the liability notice rule. *This clause is no longer in force for a straight-tip CO-151 denial on the Continence Commercial HMO Program that the current basis for such a denial settles. For every other denial that is not appealed it remains in force.*

## First-level appeal

A first-level appeal may be filed no later than the tier's first-level appeal window, in calendar days after the posting date of the denial it appeals. The count runs in calendar days from that posting date, and the last day is allowed.

| Hypothetical: 65-day window, denial posted on day 0 | Filing permitted? |
|---|---|
| day 65 | yes: the last day is allowed |
| day 66 | no |

## Second-level appeal

An appeal decision that upholds the denial posts as a new denial, whose original posting is the appeal filing. A second-level appeal may be filed only against such an upheld first-level decision, no later than the tier's second-level window in calendar days after its posting date. Where that window is 0, the tier has no customer-filed second level. On the Continence Medicare Advantage Program the plan forwards an upheld denial to the independent review entity itself.

## One appeal per level

One appeal is filed per level per denial. A denial already appealed at a level is not appealed again at that level.
